text:
ana: Heads up — after the AWQ rollout on prod-dedicated I hit intermittent OOMs on p4d pools during long-conv workloads. Pulling profiler output now.

mike: saw the same on canary. Quick glance: allocator fragmentation + repeated kernel fallback. nvprof + selector logs attached. :eyes:

ben: paste the profiler snippet when you have it.

mike: ```
kernel_selector: chose fused_attn_fp16 (req_ws=1.2GB) -> OOM -> fallback generic_attn_fp16 (req_ws=3.8GB)
gpu0 mem free: 1.5GB -> alloc burst -> OOM
allocator: slabpool, free_slabs=4, fragmentation=28%
batch_sizes observed: [1,2,16,1,8,1]
```

ravi: that pattern screams workspace sizing mismatch + aggressive batching. Long-seq request asks for large ws, allocator can't get contiguous chunk, then small frees fragment the heap.

ana: also noticed KV cache dtype for AWQ evals was left as float32 in the canary config — that doubled peak mem.

sara: kv cache float16 would cut that in half, but watch out: fused_attn kernel doesn't support fp8/packed kv in our current build. So mixed-precision paths cause kernel selector to pick the generic kernel which needs bigger temp buffers.

ben: short-term mitigations proposal: 1) cap per-request batch when seq_len > 2048, 2) enable allocator reflow when free_mem_ratio < 0.15, 3) force kv_cache dtype to fp16 for AWQ routes, 4) add a small hysteresis delay before instant kernel fallback to allow transient free to settle.

ana: any prototype?

mike: hacked a patch this morning. allocator.reflow_enabled=true, reflow_threshold=0.15, kernel_fallback_hysteresis_ms=250. Canary ran ~3h with no OOMs so far. Diff snippet:```
- if (ws_req > avail) fallback();
+ if (ws_req > avail) {
+   std::this_thread::sleep_for(200ms);
+   re-evaluate avail;
+   if (ws_req > avail) fallback();
+ }
```

ravi: nice. We should track perf impact — hysteresis will add ~200ms in worst-case before fallback, but avoids expensive kernels and reflows. Lets instrument: p95 latency, kernel_switch_count, OOM_count, avg_fragmentation.

sara: on kv dtype override: added config kv_dtype_override: "float16" per-model. Works on local but we need validation on evals for numeric regressions.

ana: plan: 1) ship allocator reflow + hysteresis to canary, 2) add batching cap for long seqs in router heuristics, 3) enforce kv_dtype_override for AWQ models in canary, 4) dashboards for kernel_switch_count + fragmentation + reflow_count. I'll open rollout ticket. :shipit:

deploy-bot: deploy requested: ticket-3452 -> canary cluster (user=ana).

ben: ack, adding dashboard tiles and alert for OOM spike (>1 in 10m).

ana: thanks all — if canary stays green for 24h we'll promote.

mike: one more note: consider a small workspace pooling strategy for fused kernels to avoid large contiguous allocs; will prototype next week.

ravi: good idea — pooling + periodic compaction might reduce fragmentation more than naive reflow.

ana: closing loop here. will post follow-up with numbers once dashboards populate.
